turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on linking sentences with and, but and because?
turns.tutor:
Hello! Good idea. We use and to add an idea, but to show a different idea, and because to give a reason. For example: I get up early because school starts at seven.

Here is a short exercise. Join the two sentences with but or because: We missed the train. We got up late.
